neighbours.label: high price or premium cost (cost more, more expensive, high-end, punches above its weight): fires on the word that marks something as costlier; the + pole is the other side, cheapness
fire: Solid oak flooring will cost more upfront, but it lasts a lifetime.
In the end, the hand-made boots were far more expensive than we expected.
Their new watch line is squarely aimed at the luxury, high-end buyer.
Eating out in Zurich is notoriously expensive for students.
Business class seats cost much more than economy on that route.
This modest sedan performs above its price class in every test.
For a small café, imported espresso machines are very costly.
Fresh salmon from Norway costs more than frozen fish.
quiet: Solid oak flooring is cheap at the moment, so we bought plenty.
In the end, the hand-made boots were cheaper than we expected.
Their new watch line is aimed at young, budget-minded buyers.
Eating out in Lisbon is surprisingly cheap for students.
Business class seats were empty on that route last Tuesday.
This modest sedan has four doors and a small boot.
For a small café, second-hand espresso machines are a bargain.
Fresh salmon from Norway arrives at the market on Mondays.

notes: Card: '- pole' ' expensive' x6, ' more' x5, ' high' x2 ('cost more', 'high-end', 'swings above its weight', Russian 'дорогое'); + pole ' cheap' x6, ' cheaper' x4, ' cheapest' x4. Probe: 'will cost more' 0.505, 'punches above its weight' 0.451, 'more expensive' 0.309, 'high-end market' 0.303, 'pricey' 0.233; cheap controls 0.004-0.012, 'larger screen' 0.144.
